item.title: OpenAI Announces Independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
OpenAI Announces Independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence

OpenAI has announced the formation of the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI), an independent panel of mathematicians tasked with advising the company and other AI firms on their interactions with mathematical research and the wider community.

🔍 Overview

The group consists of nine members described by researchers as “celebrities in the field,” including individuals with MacArthur “genius grants” and multiple Fields Medals. Members are drawn from institutions such as Oxford, Cambridge, Harvard, and Stanford. The group is hosted by the Institute for Advanced Study (IAS) in Princeton, New Jersey.

⚙️ Key Details

OpenAI has stated the following regarding the group’s operation:

  • Independence: The group will operate independently, with the freedom to make its advice public and offer advice the company has not requested.
  • Compensation: Members are not paid by OpenAI.
  • Access: The group appears it will be granted early access to OpenAI’s research.
  • Governance: The group can change its membership as it sees fit.

🧩 How it works

The AGMAI will provide guidance in several specific areas:

Focus Area Responsibility
Emerging Results Help assess significance and advise on the coordination of dissemination
Research Standards Advise on academic and professional standards of mathematical research
Tooling Advise on how tools can support mathematical research and learning

💡 Why it matters

According to the group’s website, the panel was launched as an independent group after OpenAI approached some members about establishing an external advisory board. Martin Hairer, a professor at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL) and Imperial College London, stated that the organization is “genuinely independent of OpenAI and any other of the so-called ‘frontier’ AI labs.” He noted that, aside from “obvious confidentiality requirements,” members have not signed restrictive agreements regarding public statements.

However, the development has met with some skepticism:

  • Simon Machado, a researcher at ETH Zurich, questioned the selection process for the nine members, stating the matter seemed “shrouded in mystery.”
  • Other concerns have been raised regarding whether a group of this small size possesses the breadth of expertise required to evaluate the highly specialized knowledge found at the frontiers of mathematics.
  • Francesco Fournier-Facio, an incoming professor at Heriot-Watt University, described himself as “ambivalent,” though he noted that greater engagement with mathematicians “can only make things better.”

#OpenAI #Mathematics #AGMAI #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: OpenAI wants to consult elite mathematicians about how to not fumble again

item.title: California Governor Signs Laws Regulating AI Data Center Energy and Water Use
item.description:
California Governor Signs Laws Regulating AI Data Center Energy and Water Use

California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed a package of seven bills designed to regulate the utility consumption of AI data centers and prevent them from passing costs onto residents.

⚙️ Key details

The new legislation mandates several operational requirements for data centers:

Requirement Description
Rate Classification The California Public Utilities Commission must introduce a new rate classification for data centers.
Infrastructure Costs Data centers are required to pay for upgrades to local power grids and water systems.
Transparency Proposed data centers must disclose estimated water use, energy efficiency, and drought planning to local governments.
Approval Process Facilities must meet specific energy, water, and fuel consumption requirements to qualify for a streamlined approval process.

💡 Why it matters

Governor Newsom stated that these laws aim to ensure that those profiting from data centers do not do so at the expense of residents. He noted that the regulations address community concerns regarding electricity demand, grid constraints, water use, and pollution. Additionally, the Governor signed a separate executive order last week to accelerate the creation of an AI “kill switch.”

#California #AI #DataCenters #EnergyPolicy #Regulation

Source: California tightens rules on AI data center energy and water use

item.title: Proposed Unified Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy AI and Multimodal Systems
item.description:
Proposed Unified Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy AI and Multimodal Systems

A new research paper proposes a unified evaluation framework designed to assess the trustworthiness of Large Language Models (LLMs), agentic systems, and multimodal models (MLLMs).

🔍 Overview

The framework was developed following a systematic mapping of 14,767 papers from arXiv submissions between January 2022 and August 2026. This analysis examined changes in:

  • Target systems and domains
  • Evaluation materials and conditions
  • Scoring mechanisms

Findings indicated a growing emphasis on professional applications, interaction, and action. While LLM-based scoring has increased for both agent and non-agent groups, model-generated materials have not shown a comparable sustained increase.

🧩 How it works

The framework connects cross-modal, trajectory-level, and output-level assessment through eight dimensions of trustworthiness:

Dimension Purpose
Capability Trustworthiness assessment
Robustness Trustworthiness assessment
Safety Trustworthiness assessment
Fairness Trustworthiness assessment
Transparency Trustworthiness assessment
Governance Trustworthiness assessment
Oversight Trustworthiness assessment
Efficiency Trustworthiness assessment

Additional technical features include:

  • Native Measurement Mapping: Preserves system-specific metrics while mapping them to common performance bands with traceable evidence and uncertainty estimates.
  • Meta-evaluation Layer: Examines the reproducibility, reliability, and validity of the evaluation.
  • Safety-critical Overrides: Prevents aggregate scores from masking critical failures.
  • Multidimensional Profiles: Used to expose specific strengths and weaknesses.

💡 Why it matters

The researchers state that benchmark scores alone are an incomplete basis for assessing the trustworthiness of modern AI systems. The proposed framework connects technical assessments with oversight needs by mapping to international standards, European Union regulatory requirements, and governance frameworks.

Empirical validation across deployment contexts is noted as an essential next step.

#LLM #AIEvaluation #AITrustworthiness #MultimodalAI #AgenticAI

Source: What Do We Expect from LLMs? Mapping the Design of LLM Benchmarks Source: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy Large Language Models, Agentic AI, and Multimodal Systems
